What is Odysseek?

Every place has a story. Go find it.

Odysseek is a game you play out in the real world. You get a riddle, and the answer is an actual place.

It could be a street corner in a city you've never visited, or a spot you've walked past a hundred times without really seeing it.

Figure out where the clue is pointing, go there, and the next piece of the story opens up.

One clue leads to the next, and slowly the whole story comes together.

And there's a clock running the whole time.

That moment when a riddle finally clicks, and you're already moving, is what Odysseek is really about.

It's not about one city. It's about seeing a place, or a route through it, in a way you didn't expect.

Kolkata

The Undelivered Letter

Three years ago, at the tail end of college, you and Sagnik made a promise. Once a year, the same café, the same corner table, before the city fully wakes.

Two years, two breakfasts. The jokes got older, the stories didn’t.

This morning, the chair across from you stays empty. The coffee goes cold. His phone rings and rings into nothing. Sagnik has never once been late.

Then your phone lights up. An email from him, with nothing in it but a single line, Don’t order breakfast yet, and a riddle.

Why isn’t he here? Why write when he could call? And since when does Sagnik care for riddles?

Somewhere out in the waking city, someone is waiting for you to find out.

  • 4 stops
  • Across Heart of South Kolkata
  • Walking and Auto Rides
  • Tourist-friendly

Scene 1

Three years ago, in the last week of college, you and Sagnik made a promise.

No matter where life took you, no matter how busy things got, you’d meet once a year at Cafe X. Same day. Same table. Before the city fully wakes up.

You’ve kept that promise twice. Two years of long breakfasts, bad jokes and “remember when” stories that never got old.

Today is the third.

You get there early, take the corner table by the window, and order a coffee. The street outside is still half asleep.

7:15. Sagnik isn’t here yet.

7:25. Still no Sagnik.

You call. It rings out. That’s strange, because in two years Sagnik has never missed this. Not once.

7:30. Your coffee is going cold.

Then your phone buzzes.

1 new email

From: Sagnik

Don’t order breakfast yet.

Don’t order breakfast yet.

Scene 2

Gariahat crossing.

Of course. Char matha.

You stare at the screen. Why isn’t Sagnik picking up? And what is this, a riddle? Seriously?

But you know the place. And you know exactly what Sagnik would want you to find there.

Bedouin Sher-E-Bengal.

Chicken rolls, every other day in college. Paper-wrapped, too much onion, always eaten standing up. If Sagnik wanted to meet anywhere, it would be there.

But why? What is he up to?

You grab your bag.

Fine, Sagnik. I’ll play along!

Scene 3

Dakshinapan. Dhakuria.

Right. Of course.

And suddenly you’re tasting it. Mishti fuchka. Tok-jhal-mishti aloo dum. Eaten standing outside the complex, with the bill never quite adding up.

Rajendra Fuchka.

Forty-odd years old, and still there every single day. Some things in this city refuse to change.

You remember the three of you crowded around that stall, fighting over who got the last piece of aloo dum.

And then, out of nowhere, a thought slips in.

Her.

How did I ever forget about her?

Scene 4

Lokenath Paper House.

Of course.

Every first of the month, the three of you came here to stock up. Notebooks, refills, highlighters you’d lose by the 10th.

She bargained like it was a sport. Somehow she always knocked ten whole rupees off the total. Ten rupees! She’d walk out grinning like she’d won a war.

And Sagnik was always there, quietly paying your share on the months you were short. He never once made it awkward.

You look down at the pen clipped to your shirt pocket.

She gave you that. On convocation day.

So many memories, all coming back at once.

Let’s see this place again.

Scene 5

Reminiscing the Past

The same noise. The same crowd. The same notebooks stacked high at the front.

And on the steps outside the shop, sipping a cup of tea, Sagnik.

Your eyes meet.

Sagnik bursts out laughing. Not a smile, a proper, can’t-breathe laugh.

“Sagnik. You made me run across half of South Kolkata. Riddles? Seriously? Why did you make me work so hard?”

Sagnik keeps laughing. Then he wipes his eyes, reaches into his bag, and holds out an envelope.

You take it.

It’s addressed to you. To Som.

You know the handwriting! You have seen it before!

Lumi.

“How had I almost forgotten about her, in all these busy years?”

Scene 7

Som,

If you’re reading this, you solved every clue. I knew you would. You always did.

Do you still carry the pen? I hope so.

I have something to tell you. I should have said it three years ago, and I didn’t, and I’ve regretted it ever since. I won’t write it here. Some things shouldn’t be read off paper.

One more clue. Last one. Then you’ll have the answer.

Lumi

Final riddle

Moha-te shuru, maya-te shesh, naam-er tolay chena desh,

Garia theke auto dhoro, aar baki nei besh.

Two little words begin the name: "moha", then "maya" too,

Add "tola", a Bengali word, and the place appears to you.

Reach Garia first, then hail an auto for a short ride more,

A sweet shop waits there, loved for its kochuri, hot and warm.

Name the place.

The END

Solved it!

Sagnik, I’ll see you soon.

I have to go see about a girl.

Mohamaya Tola.

The sweet shop is exactly where it always was.

And at the corner table, with a plate of hot kochuri in front of her, is Lumi.

Your eyes meet.

She smiles.

“I knew you’d solve every riddle I gave you. Not just today, but back in college too. You just loved riddles, didn’t you?”

Everything comes back rushing.

You met her in first year. She was your friend. Our friend. The three of you, always together: Sagnik’s jokes, her laugh, your quiet habit of watching her a second too long.

She loved detective thrillers. Mysteries, riddles. She told you about every one of them, every single time, whether you asked or not. And she loved riddles. She’d leave you one at the end of every adda and refuse to give the answer.

That’s why the clues.

It was never Sagnik. It was her.

Then you remember the first time it was just the two of you.

Dakshinapan, where she needed a dress altered. You carried her bags and pretended to be bored.

Gariahat, where you shared a chicken roll at Bedouin, standing up, too much onion.

Ruby, because that’s where she caught her bus home to Garia. You watched it pull away and stood there far longer than you needed to.

You look at the envelope again.

Ruby. Gariahat. Dakshinapan.

She sent you back through that day, backwards.

Over time, it only got worse. Or better. You were never sure which.

By the end of third year, you finally had your chance. Just the two of you, nothing in the way.

And you couldn’t say it.

There was something between you, a chemistry you could feel in your veins, and you were sure it was only on your side. You never said a word.

That day still comes back to you at night. The words ready, and your mouth refusing.

You feel your face go warm.

She pushes the second plate across the table.

“Baki kotha-gulo kochuri khete khete boli?”

Your choice: B

You fold the letter along its creases and slide it back into the envelope.

Your hands are steady. Mostly.

Sagnik has stopped laughing. He watches you for a moment, then nudges the other cup of tea across the step.

“You sure?”

You think about it. About Ruby, Gariahat, and a bus pulling away.

“Yeah,” you say. “I think I’m good.”

Sagnik doesn’t push. He never did. He just shrugs, grins, and steals a sip of your tea like old times.

The street hums around you. Tea, steam, someone haggling over a notebook.

Somewhere out there, there’s a sweet shop and a table you’ll never sit at. And somewhere in your pocket, a pen that still works.

You tuck the envelope into your bag.

Some stories wait.

This one will still be here.

    How it Works

    01. Choose Your Adventure

    Begin by selecting your preferred exploration mode. Whether you're a local who knows the city or a tourist discovering a city or place for the first time, Odysseek offers an experience suited to you.

    • Local Mode: Challenging riddles with minimal hints.
    • Tourist Mode: Guided clues, helpful hints, food recommendations and directions.

    02. Decode the Clue

    Every adventure begins with a riddle inspired by a real location. Read between the lines, connect historical references, cultural details and geographical hints, and figure out where the clue is leading you.

    03. Explore the City

    Once you have identified the location, head out and explore! Navigate through streets, discover hidden gems and experience familiar places from an entirely new perspective.

    04. Verify Your Arrival

    Reaching the destination is not enough. You need to verify that you've actually arrived. Odysseek uses your phone's location to check your proximity to the designated spot. Once your arrival is successfully verified, the adventure progresses.

    05. Unlock the Next Chapter

    Successfully completing a location unlocks your next clue. Each solved riddle takes you further into the adventure, encouraging you to explore more of the city and uncover its stories one destination at a time.

    06. Experience a location Differently

    The journey is more than just solving riddles. Discover local culture, heritage, interesting landmarks and food spots while turning an ordinary city visit into an interactive adventure.

    Every clue has a story. Every destination has a secret.

    With Odysseek, don't just visit a city. Decode it, discover it and experience it.
